summary.oneLiner: Laxmi Dental delivered a strong Q4FY26 recovery with record revenue (INR 74cr, +22% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins (18.3%) despite US tariff headwinds, driven by robust international lab growth (+40.9%) and strategic scanner deployment. The launch of iScope 360 and normalization of US tariffs to 10% position the company for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion in FY27.

one-line thesis: Laxmi Dental delivered a strong Q4FY26 recovery with record revenue (INR 74cr, +22% YoY) and expanded EBITDA margins (18.3%) despite US tariff headwinds, driven by robust international lab growth (+40.9%) and strategic scanner deployment. The launch of iScope 360 and normalization of US tariffs to 10% position the company for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 74cr (Q4, +22% YoY), INR 277.9cr (FY26, +16.2% YoY); EBITDA: INR 13.5cr (Q4, +41.8% YoY), Margin 18.3% (vs 15.7% prior year); PAT: INR 10.1cr (Q4, reported), includes INR 1.3cr tax benefit from one-time gratuity adjustment recognized in Q3; Normalized PAT margin ~12%; Order Book: Not explicitly disclosed, but scanner deployments (211 units in Q4, 1009 in FY26) act as leading indicators for lab/aligner volume; Net Debt: Zero (Cash & Investments ~INR 99cr).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Management targets similar trajectory to past years (16-24% range) over next 2-3 years, contingent on market conditions; Margins: Aims to improve beyond Q4 levels (18.3% EBITDA) via operating leverage and automation, though no specific FY27 guidance given; Order Inflow: Positive momentum expected from scanner-driven digital penetration (targeting >90%); Capex: Planned deployment of remaining IPO proceeds based on operational needs, following INR 18.4cr spend in FY26.
order book & pipeline: Scanner deployments serve as proxy for future order flow: 211 units in Q4FY26, 1,009 units in FY26. 80% of domestic lab impressions now digital, targeting 90%.
segment / subsidiary detail: Dental Lab: INR 45.9cr (+27% YoY), Domestic +16.3%, International +40.9%; Aligners (Bizdent): Recovered in Q4 (+10.9% YoY), focus on margin preservation over volume; Raw Material (Vedia): INR 7.3cr, stable sequentially, impacted by March freight costs but strong YoY; Pediatric (Kids-e-Dental): INR 5.4cr; Scanners: Strategic low-margin enabler driving core business growth.
growth verticals / optionality: iScope 360 (remote monitoring/consultation) creates new B2B2C revenue stream (device sales + subscription points); International expansion beyond US (currently 20% of revenue) into new geographies; Consolidation opportunities in fragmented domestic market using INR 99cr cash reserve; Regulatory approvals for Kids-e-Dental in EU/US.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 70.5% (Q4), ~76% excluding scanners; EBITDA Margin: 18.3% (Q4), impacted by ~74bps from US tariffs in early quarter; Cost structure benefits from operating leverage as people costs remain stable while revenue scales; Automation investments expected to further decouple cost growth from revenue.
capex / expansion: INR 18.4cr incurred in FY26; Future capex to be funded by remaining IPO proceeds, aligned with revenue growth and automation/digitalization initiatives.
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet with INR 99cr cash/investments; Open to M&A (labs, IP, tech) if value-accretive opportunities arise; Continued investment in R&D (AI, digital platforms) and geographic expansion.
risks & watch-items: US Tariff volatility (though normalized to 10%); Intense competition in domestic aligner market leading to pricing pressure; Regulatory delays for international product approvals (Kids-e-Dental); Freight cost fluctuations impacting export timelines; Execution risk on scanner deployment conversion to lab/aligner orders.
management quality / tone: Confident and resilient; Emphasizes long-term strategy over short-term noise; Balanced approach to growth vs. margins; Transparent on challenges (tariffs, freight) but optimistic about structural trends (digital dentistry, under-penetrated Indian market).
non-obvious takeaways: Scanner business is intentionally low-margin to drive high-margin lab/aligner stickiness; iScope 360 creates a 'lock-in' effect where patients are tied to specific dentists via the platform, enhancing dentist loyalty and recurring revenue potential; US tariff impact was front-loaded in Q4 and largely resolved by quarter-end, suggesting Q1FY27 could see even stronger margins.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US tariff reduction from punitive levels to 10% and strong international lab growth | Laxmi Dental Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of tariff normalization and diversified global footprint; Q4 results validate resilience. |
| Intensifying competition and pricing pressure in domestic aligner market | Unlisted/Funded Domestic Aligner Startups | loser | Med | Laxmi's focus on margin preservation and integrated model (lab + aligner + scanner) may squeeze smaller, less diversified competitors. |
| Adoption of digital dentistry and remote monitoring tools | Dentists using Laxmi's ecosystem | beneficiary | High | Access to iScope 360 and scanners enhances their service offering, patient retention, and operational efficiency. |

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described (per the F&S Report) as 'India's only end to end integrated dental products company', with a comparison grid showing it as the sole company covering custom-made fixed prosthesis, removable prosthesis, clear aligners, aligner sheet, thermo-forming machine, intraoral scanner and paediatric crowns.
- Claims to be the 'Second largest player in domestic laboratory business and largest export laboratory', and separately the 'largest and most profitable B2B2C indigenous dental aligner company' and 'The only Indian co. specialized in paediatric dental products'.
- B2B2C direct-connect model with 22,000+ dental clinics, dental companies and dentists across 320+ cities and 95+ countries; deck argues successful global aligner companies are doctor-led/B2B2C while D2C models 'have struggled to establish in the market'.
- Cites the Indian lab market as highly fragmented (<50 large labs with INR 25-100+ Cr annual revenue vs >5,000 medium labs at INR 1-25 Cr) with a regulatory-driven shift from unorganised to organised labs.
- States it is a 'Preferred partner for one of the largest DSO in the USA indicating headroom for significant expansion of network', and the 'First Indian Company to get US FDA 510K approval' in aligners.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation] Inclusion of dental crowns, bridges and resins as a Class B risk Medical Device by CDSCO, plus ISO 13485 compliance and a valid CDSCO licence, is presented as the driver of growth of the organised dental lab network.
- [Accounting/JV] As per Ind AS, reported revenue excludes Kids-e-Dental and IDBG AI Dent as jointly controlled entities; 'Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Reported EBITDA + ESOP expenses (non-cash in nature). + 60% of Kids-e-dental PAT + 49% of IDBG AI Dent PAT' (the FY-series version also adds IDS event expense recorded in Q4FY25).
- [Exceptional/labour code] FY26 carries an Exceptional Item of -57.8 mn; the deck notes a tax benefit of INR 13 Mn in Q4FY26 'related to the one-time exceptional item on gratuity expense in Q3FY26 due to changes in labour code'.
- [Certifications] Facilities/products carry ISO 13485:2016, ISO 45001:2018, CDSCO, US FDA, Regulation EU 2017/745 and 510(k) US FDA; the aligner-materials business holds a Certificate of conformity under Regulation EU 2017/745.
- [Listing/history] Journey began in 1989 with a small dental lab; incorporated July 2004 as 'Laxmi Dental Export Private Limited'; listed on Indian stock exchanges on January 20, 2025.
